transcript:
This message comes from Kachava. A little boost goes a long way, especially when it comes to caring for your gut during the holiday season and beyond.
Introducing Kachava's new 3-in-1 digestive boost. Simply mix into your favorite Kachava shake or any cold beverage.
Go to kachava.com and use code NPR for 15% off your first order. That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A dot com. Code NPR.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. President Trump is spending the Thanksgiving holiday at his club in Palm Beach where he signed a disaster declaration for Florida following days of relentless rain.
It's been raining continuously. It's the craziest thing. It's stopped now. Very unusual for Florida, but it's record-setting rains in a lot of areas in Florida.
We're beating up pretty badly and we're releasing immediate funding.
Parts of Florida's east coast has been deluged with rain this month, and Florida's St. John's River rose to record levels.
Meanwhile, that Thanksgiving Day storm has knocked out power to hundreds of thousands of homes and businesses on the east coast. Coastal flooding has affected areas from North Carolina to New York.
California has also faced coastal flooding, and Missouri and Illinois got socked by heavy snow.
President Trump told reporters at Mar-a-Lago that Russian leader Vladimir Putin can come to next month's G20 meeting in Florida if he wants to.
The two are reported to have discussed the G20 when they met in China last week. The Kremlin says no decision's been made.
President Trump's son-in-law and peace envoy, Jared Kushner, says Putin has "shown restraint" in the war against Ukraine by not using nuclear weapons.
Kushner was speaking on a podcast hosted by the CEO of the company that owns Politico. That's Villa Marx Reports.
On the MD Meets podcast with Axel Springer chief, Matias Dovner, Kushner called Putin "a grandmaster of politics" and credited him with holding himself back.
"So far Putin has showed restraint. He's agreed not to use nuclear weapons, which obviously is a big thing, and he's reassured us that that's not his intention."
Kushner said he believes Putin wants peace between Russia and Ukraine. He also said peace talks should focus most of all on ending the war, not deciding which side is right or wrong.
But this little sign the war itself is winding down. Ukrainian president Vladimir Zelensky said in his nightly address to the nation Thursday that Russia was preparing a new mass strike in the coming days.
He also urged Ukrainians to pay attention to missile alerts. For NPR News, I'm Villa Marx.
Artificial intelligence expected to play a big role in holiday shopping this year. The National Retail Federation says almost 60 percent of shoppers plan to use AI this weekend. NPR's Stephen Pissassa has some tips.
Traditional online shopping is all about finding the right keyword. AI shopping is more about vibes.
The conversations you can have are here's a style that I know my cousin is into and I need to find a gift for them.
Emily Pfeiffer, a forester, advises retailers about AI commerce. She says just remember when writing an AI prompt to be as specific and clear as possible.
It's best if you imagine that it's a young child who will probably misinterpret your request.
Pfeiffer also warns you should not assume AI will find you the best price. Like with human shoppers, AI needs time for deal hunting.
And be careful what private data you share with AI. Stephen Pissassa, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency says it expects test results from samples taken after Wednesday's controlled detonation of degraded bomb-making material in Iowa to come in soon.
The EPA says results could come in as soon as tomorrow. The agency says it took more than 1,500 samples of air, water, soil and dust before the detonation and hundreds after it.
Authorities in New Mexico on the lookout for a pregnant inmate to escape by stealing a corrections transport vehicle.
The state corrections department says three officers who accompanied 26-year-old Rebecca Taylor were stopped at a restaurant Wednesday when she climbed into the driver's seat and drove away.
Officials say she was unrestrained due to her pregnancy. An enthusiastic black and tan Coonhound named Rocker as top dog of this year's national dog show, NPR's Chloe Veltman, reports on Rocker's victory over six other group winners to take Best in Show.
Rocker's handler Mandy Clevenger told NBC the Coonhound had a great time at the 2026 national dog show.
Rocker loves the crowd. He loves the people, loves other dogs and kids. So this is a great venue for him.
Best in Show judge Lorraine Bisso praised Rocker's handsome looks and physical prowess.
She also commended Clevenger for fading into the background and allowing the dog to shine, a remarkable feat considering the fact the handler was wearing a bright yellow suit.
The annual event was held in person at the Greater Philadelphia Expo Center earlier this month.
NBC has telecasted each year on Thanksgiving Day since 2002. Owing to the rescheduled Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, NBC plans to re-air the show on Saturday starting at noon. Chloe Veltman, NPR News.
And I'm Joel Snyder. This is NPR.
This message comes from IXL. IXL provides personalized learning and powerful insights that help teachers boost achievement and understand student progress in real time.
Learn more at IXL.com/NPR.
